claims.claim: Hong Kong should not impose a hard cap on initial rents in subdivided units.
Hong Kong should tighten the existing tenancy-control regime by extending security of tenure and adding a light, indexed band on initial rents.
Enforcement capacity should be redirected toward the queue and toward conditions.
The long-run elasticity of marginal SDU-type supply to controlled rents is estimated at 0.31 to 0.48.
A 10 percent cap-induced reduction removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years.
First-generation controls show consistent supply contraction, while second-generation controls show small or null effects.
Hong Kong's 2021 ordinance is second-generation, and stock grew from 100,800 units in 2019 to 111,200 in 2025.
A hard cap would move Hong Kong into the first-generation category, where contraction evidence is consistent.
In the modelled tightened-cap scenario, a 15 percent cut in initial rents yields a net transfer of about 900 dollars per month to incumbents.
The tightened-cap scenario leaves 3,000 to 4,000 households per year unable to enter the segment, mostly new arrivals and newly formed households.
Berlin's initial-offer rents fell sharply but listing supply contracted within a year as owners withheld or rerouted flats.
When Berlin's law was struck down, suppressed increases released above the pre-cap trend line.
Mr Chan fears landlords would rather convert units back to storage under a hard cap.
Mr Chan says he would accept any rent if the queue were three years instead of five and a half.
In the NGO survey of 440 households, 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure.
In the NGO survey, 74 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for a faster public-housing offer.
Mrs Wong has lived in an SDU for nine years and has never received a written tenancy agreement.
Two flats in Mrs Wong's stairwell were converted to non-residential storage after the ordinance, contradicting her belief that landlords cannot exit.
Current inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year.
A band-based initial-rent cap requires a certifiable tenancy register estimated at 40 to 60 staff-years to stand up.
The subcommittee could not identify any enforcement design under which the newest-arrival tail is protected first rather than last.
A hard cap framed as deprivation of income stream would almost certainly attract compensation claims under the Basic Law.
Contractual-term regulation sits on firmer legal ground but leaves initial rent unregulated.
Counsel's published per-square-foot band is legally safer and consistent with the NGO's preferred narrow tightening.
The stable stock under the 2021 ordinance is an artifact of a non-binding instrument, and a binding one behaves differently.
Hong Kong should tighten tenure security and add a defensible, indexed initial-rent band, paired with genuine queue reduction and condition enforcement.
A hard cap would transfer income to today's incumbents while shrinking the stock, missing the newest arrivals, and consuming enforcement capacity that conditions inspection needs more.
